note: Page configuration, not a record. The one-page brief for model providers and brokers (vp-grow-odin-r-d bundle-4 WO-01, WO-VG-05). Claim texts hold no digits and no number words; each {name} is a value read from the cited experiment record by a JSON pointer (scripts/lab-pages.mjs) and linked to it. A claim's record must be a measured experiment record with a decided verdict: the router-arm records (EXP 018, verdict incomplete; EXP 019, results published but not yet summarised here) are never a claim's record, only an item in notResults. No broker or lead is named on this page; brokers appear by the letters their published records use. scripts/provider-brief-export.mjs renders the same claims as Markdown for the seed deck.

claims.text: We sent identical requests for the same model through the brokers we use, at the same moment: {calls} counted calls. For {modelS}, the median billed price was {aS} times the list price through Broker A, {bS} through Broker B and {cS} through Broker C. For {modelM} it was {aM}, {bM} and {cM}. No broker answered with a different model than the model asked for: {subS} silent substitutions for {modelS} and {subM} for {modelM}.

On a sealed corpus of private changes, reviewed by every model through the same tool-free seat, the cheapest model, {cheapModel}, cost {cheapCost} per review and caught {cheapCaught} of {cheapOf} seeded defects; the dearest, {dearModel}, cost {dearCost} per review and caught {dearCaught} of {dearOf}. The catch intervals of all models in the experiment overlap, so on this corpus the price of a review varied far more than what it caught.
